LandingPage.intro1: Music that truly moves people usually carries several layers at once: precise rhythmic structure (the physical layer), rigorously considered arrangement logic (the structural layer), depth that confronts emotional ups and downs (the emotional layer), and energy that rises and falls in balance (the vitality layer).
LandingPage.intro2: Computable Beauty tries to translate this four-dimensional aesthetic intuition into computable dimensions.

extracting.label: Acoustic Feature Extraction
extracting.detail: Computes spectrum, beat grid, key/pitch distribution, and dynamic envelope from the waveform, producing the base feature vector for later analysis

classifying.label: Multi-Task Semantic Classification
classifying.detail: Infers genre, valence/arousal, and instrumentation in parallel, while detecting chord progressions and section boundaries

scoring.label: Four-Dimensional Aesthetic Scoring
scoring.detail: Independently quantifies physical precision, structural logic, emotional depth, and vital tension based on the acoustic and classification results

explaining.label: AI Evidence-Based Interpretation
explaining.detail: An LLM generates a written analysis grounded in the structured output of the previous layers, with every conclusion traceable back to a specific metric

physical_precision.label: Physical
physical_precision.description: Quantifies the physical precision of performance and production from tempo stability, dynamic range, and spectral balance.
physical_precision.formula: score = (tempo stability score × 0.4 + dynamic range score × 0.3 + spectral balance score × 0.3) × 100
physical_precision.breakdown:
tempo stability score = 1 − min(tempo stability ÷ 0.13, 1); closer to 0 is more stable, caps at 0 past 0.13s
dynamic range score = clamp((dynamic range − 5) ÷ 20, 0, 1); linear between 5-25dB
spectral balance score = 1 − clamp(spectral std ÷ 25, 0, 1); a smaller std is more balanced

structural_logic.label: Logic
structural_logic.description: Measures whether the music's structure forms a coherent, non-repetitive whole from T-S-D function coverage, section duration balance, and chord vocabulary richness.
structural_logic.formula: score = (T-S-D coverage score × 0.3 + section balance score × 0.3 + chord richness score × 0.4) × 100
structural_logic.breakdown:
T-S-D coverage score = T-S-D coverage itself (already a 0-1 ratio, no rescaling)
section balance score = 1 − clamp(section duration std ÷ mean ÷ 2, 0, 1); less dispersion is more balanced
chord richness score = clamp(distinct chord count ÷ 24, 0, 1); 24 is madmom's full chord vocabulary size

emotional_depth.label: Emotion
emotional_depth.description: Measures the completeness of emotional movement from the valence arc's peak-to-valley range, arousal dispersion, and polarity shift rate.
emotional_depth.formula: score = (valence range score × 0.4 + arousal dispersion score × 0.3 + polarity shift score × 0.3) × 100
emotional_depth.breakdown:
valence range score = clamp(valence range ÷ 1.0, 0, 1)
arousal dispersion score = clamp(arousal std ÷ 0.15, 0, 1)
polarity shift score = clamp(shift rate ÷ 0.025, 0, 1); a rate, not the raw shift count

vital_tension.label: Vitality
vital_tension.description: Measures how strongly the music's energy rises, falls, and drives forward, from loudness contrast across structural sections and rhythmic burst density.
vital_tension.formula: score = (loudness contrast score × 0.5 + burst density score × 0.5) × 100
vital_tension.breakdown:
loudness contrast score = clamp(loudness contrast ÷ 0.29, 0, 1)
burst density score = clamp(burst density ÷ 310, 0, 1)

EvidenceLabel.tempo_stability: Tempo Stability (standard deviation of inter-beat intervals, in seconds, lower = more stable)
EvidenceLabel.frequency_balance_std_db: Spectral Balance (standard deviation of mean energy across low/mid/high bands, in dB, lower = more balanced)
EvidenceLabel.dynamic_range_db: Dynamic Range (95th vs. 5th percentile loudness ratio, in dB, with silent edges trimmed)
EvidenceLabel.tsd_coverage: T-S-D Function Coverage (share of chord events that are a tonic/subdominant/dominant function, higher = more conventional)
EvidenceLabel.segment_balance_ratio: Section Duration Balance (coefficient of variation of segment durations — standard deviation over mean, lower = more balanced)
EvidenceLabel.n_distinct_chords: Chord Vocabulary Size (number of distinct chords across the track, more = richer harmony)
EvidenceLabel.valence_delta: Emotional Arc Range (difference between the valence arc's max and min)
EvidenceLabel.polarity_switches: Emotional Polarity Shifts (count of hysteresis-band crossings from negative to positive or back, not raw adjacent-frame flips)
EvidenceLabel.polarity_switch_rate: Emotional Polarity Shift Rate (shift count normalized by arc length, so longer tracks aren't favored just for having more sample points)
EvidenceLabel.arousal_std: Arousal Dispersion (standard deviation of the arousal arc)
EvidenceLabel.dynamic_contrast: Loudness Dynamic Contrast (difference between the loudest and quietest structural section's own mean loudness)
EvidenceLabel.burst_density: Energy Burst Frequency (number of local onset-strength maxima, per minute)

arousal.label: Arousal
arousal.description: The activation intensity dimension of emotion, reflecting the level of psychophysiological arousal — higher values indicate stronger physiological activation and alertness; lower values trend toward calm and relaxed.
arousal.computation: Extracts an embedding with msd-musicnn, feeding a regression head trained on the DEAM dataset, then linearly rescales the model's 1-9 raw prediction to 0~1.

valence.label: Valence
valence.description: The positive/negative polarity dimension of emotion, representing how pleasant the emotional experience is — positive values correspond to a positive, pleasant emotional tone, negative values to a negative, low tone, with 0 being neutral.
valence.computation: Reuses the same msd-musicnn embedding pipeline as arousal, feeding a regression head trained on the DEAM dataset, then linearly rescales the model's 1-9 raw prediction to -1~1.

tension.label: Tension
tension.description: The sensory dissonance (roughness) of the music's sound itself — higher values mean the pitch combinations are more physically dissonant, sounding more suspended and in need of resolution.
tension.computation: Computed frame-by-frame from spectral peaks using a sensory dissonance algorithm (Plomp & Levelt, 1965), averaged across the track and normalized.

release.label: Release
release.description: How much the dissonance settles down right after a tension peak — higher values mean a sharper drop following the peak, sounding more like the tension has actually been released.
release.computation: Finds local peaks on the same frame-level dissonance curve used for tension, averages the drop in a short window right after each peak, then normalizes.

energy.label: Energy
energy.description: The overall drive and impact of the music, driven jointly by loudness and rhythmic density — higher values mean louder energetic passages and denser hits and attacks.
energy.computation: Loudness is the 90th percentile of the track's RMS, rhythmic density is the frequency of local onset-strength peaks, the two are weighted equally.
energy.formula:
energy = loudness score × 0.5 + burst density score × 0.5
loudness score = clamp(RMS 90th percentile ÷ 0.50, 0, 1)
burst density score = clamp(burst density ÷ 310, 0, 1)
